# How to Indent HTML and PHP Code in Notepad++

Notepad++ handles code indentation through a combination of syntax highlighting, folding capabilities, and configurable formatting rules. While the editor provides a visual representation of your code structure, automatically reflowing text to match that structure requires specific settings within its configuration files. Understanding how these settings interact is essential for maintaining clean HTML and PHP code without manual intervention every time you hit the "Format" button.

The primary mechanism for automatic indentation in Notepad++ is defined by the `indentation` section of the user configuration file, typically located at `%APPDATA%\Notepad++\config-default.ini` or within a custom settings file like `notepad++.ini`. To enable this feature globally, you must ensure the `defaultIndent` option is set correctly. For HTML and PHP, which often rely on specific nesting levels (such as 2 spaces for divs or classes), setting `defaultIndent=2` ensures that every time you type a closing tag followed by an opening tag on a new line, the cursor jumps to the correct column.

However, simply enabling default indentation is rarely sufficient for complex files containing mixed PHP and HTML logic. The editor needs to recognize the language mode to apply the correct rules. You can verify this by checking the bottom status bar of the Notepad++ window; it should display "HTML" or "PHP" rather than a generic "Plain text." If you are working with a file that switches between languages, such as a PHP script containing HTML blocks, ensure that the language detection is active. Notepad++ uses regex patterns to identify these blocks, and if your code structure deviates from standard conventions (for example, missing closing braces or unusual comment styles), the editor might fail to indent correctly.

For immediate visual organization, utilizing the built-in "Reindent All" command is often more effective than relying solely on default settings during a coding session. You can access this feature via the `Edit` menu by selecting `Indentation > Reindent All`. This command analyzes the current cursor position and the surrounding context, pushing lines to the correct indentation level based on their folding structure. To use this effectively, you must first enable line folding. In Notepad++, click the small arrow next to the language name in the status bar or go to `Language > HTML` (or PHP) to ensure the parser is active. Once folded, collapsing sections allows the editor to understand the hierarchy of elements, making "Reindent All" significantly smarter.

When dealing with large projects involving both HTML and PHP, manual formatting can become tedious. In such cases, integrating an external formatter like `PHP-CS-Fixer` or `Prettier` via a plugin is a robust solution. Notepad++ supports plugins that can bridge this gap, allowing you to run command-line formatters directly within the editor. This approach decouples the formatting logic from the editor's own configuration, ensuring consistency across different machines and team members. The trade-off here is increased setup complexity; you must install the necessary dependencies and configure the plugin settings in Notepad++'s `plugins.cfg`.

Another common pitfall involves line endings. If your file uses Windows-style CRLF line endings on a Unix-based server or editor, indentation markers might appear misaligned. Always ensure your project uses a consistent line ending style, preferably LF, especially if you are collaborating with teams using version control systems like Git. You can change this globally in Notepad++ by navigating to `Settings > Preferences > Format` and unchecking "Convert tabs to spaces" if you prefer tabs, or setting the number of spaces per tab explicitly.

For advanced users managing complex PHP templates where HTML and PHP logic are tightly intertwined, relying on the default folding might not capture the logical blocks correctly. In these scenarios, manually marking regions using the `Mark region` feature (`Ctrl+Shift+Alt+M`) can help Notepad++ understand specific code blocks as distinct units for indentation purposes. This manual intervention ensures that even non-standard code structures respect the desired formatting rules.

If you are building a Laravel application or working on similar PHP frameworks, consider leveraging tools specifically designed for that ecosystem. The Laravel company offers resources and documentation that often align well with modern development workflows. While Notepad++ is a powerful standalone editor, integrating it with framework-specific linters and formatters can provide the best of both worlds: local editing speed with automated quality enforcement.

Ultimately, achieving perfect indentation in Notepad++ requires balancing global configuration settings with context-aware commands. By configuring `defaultIndent`, enabling folding, and utilizing "Reindent All" or external plugins, you can maintain high-quality code structure without sacrificing workflow efficiency.
